title: SCNet P0 R06j 800 m/s fragment Johnson-Cook erosion isolation
purpose: Isolate whether the unavailable R06i response is caused by deletion of failed fragment elements, while keeping the terminal TSSFAC=0.05 policy and every other model field frozen.

provenance.identity_rule: Mesh, coordinates, connectivity, IDs, PIDs, post-explosion initial state, material strength and failure coefficients, EOS, contact, section, boundaries, speed, termination, timestep, output cards and resources remain identical to Job 72740022. Only fragment MAT_015 Card 4 EROD changes 0 to 1.
provenance.factor_scope: fragment MAT_015 Card 4 field 3 EROD only, 0 to 1

symmetry.validity: normal incidence, face-on cube, centered impact only

shared_measurement_upgrade.database_extent_binary_policy: Set NEIPH=6 and explicitly preserve all other R15.0.2 documented Card 1/Card 2 defaults; Card 2 is mandatory.

damage_source.sentinel_policy: absolute value at or above 1e29 is unavailable with a reason, never zero

shared_measurement_upgrade.database_extent_d3part_policy: Explicit NEIPH=6 request is a redundant-channel experiment; full D3PLOT HVAR6 remains authoritative.

paired_experiments.question: Does suppressing fragment element erosion remove the upstream deleted-mass mechanism while Johnson-Cook damage/failure evidence remains observable?

preregistered_evaluation.single_factor_rule: The R06j deck may differ from the returned R06i deck only in TITLE and fragment material MAT_015 Card 4 field 3 EROD, 0 to 1. Plate EROD remains 0.

solver_semantics.erod_0: element erosion is allowed after failure (default)
solver_semantics.erod_nonzero: the failed element is not eroded; its deviatoric stresses are set to zero after failure
solver_semantics.source: ANSYS LS-DYNA Materials Manual R14, MAT_015 Card 4 EROD

interpretation_rules.deletion_suppressed_with_failure_damage_: supports fragment failure erosion as the cause of the upstream deletion mechanism only
interpretation_rules.negative_volume_or_solver_failure: supports numerical dependence on erosion but does not validate the material or contact model
interpretation_rules.primary_qoi_policy: never promote EROD=1 response values to physical labels, calibration targets or reference data

submission_sequence.wave_0_gate: Zero KEY errors, 1 node/32 ranks, no mass scaling, readable D3PART/full-D3PLOT HVAR6/NCFORC, and a formal comparison with Job 72740022. Solver failure/negative volume is retained as diagnostic evidence.
submission_sequence.hold_after_wave_0: Do not release 2000 m/s, treatments, fitting or labels. Audit the single-factor erosion mechanism first.
submission_sequence.resource_identity: Use exactly one node, 32 ranks, LS-DYNA R15 MPP double precision, and the same memory settings as Job 72740022.

deferred_not_generated.reason: Denied by the terminal timestep stop rule.
Hold until the deletion mechanism is resolved.

claim_boundary: R06i established local timestep consistency but not response availability.
R06j changes only the fragment material EROD flag from 0 to 1; plate erosion remains enabled with EROD=0.
EROD=1 intentionally changes the post-failure numerical treatment and is diagnostic, not a physical treatment.
The model continues to start from the same post-explosion fragment state.
Neither static PASS nor a normal R06j termination authorizes engine fitting, damage-tree fitting or dataset admission.

explosion_instant_start_policy.r06h_rule: initial geometry, velocity and all other state remain byte-equivalent to Job 72639935
explosion_instant_start_policy.future_full_warhead_rule: A full-warhead high-fidelity model may start at explosion time only after the mapped mass, momentum, energy, fragment-state and boundary-state transfer is frozen and audited.
